messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] 5xx spike on inference.redwoodapi.com in us-west-2a — high connection resets and increased tail latency. Aggregated error rate: 18% over the last 5m. Trigger: inference-p50>250ms && 5xx_rate>10%. Pager: @Alice Chen oncall.
Alice Chen: ACK — I'm on it. spinning up workspace. Can someone grab NLB & ENI metrics?
Ben Ortiz: Looking at VPC flow logs now. Seeing a lot of TCP RSTs from instances in us-west-2a around 12:03:22 UTC. No obvious ELB target failover yet.
Carla Nguyen: Runtime SRE — KV cache error bursts correlated with pod restarts. Getting OOM-kill-ish logs in kube events for model-serving nodes in us-west-2a.
Dinesh Patel: Product/ingest — customer telemetry shows timeout errors for a subset of long-context requests only. Might be path MTU or packet drops causing retransmits.
Iris Morgan: Support — flagged a couple of premium customers seeing degraded response times. Not full outages but elevated errors. They asked if we have a mitigation ETA.
Alice Chen: Initial plan: 1) reroute traffic off us-west-2a to other AZs for affected endpoints, 2) scale up dedicated capacity in us-west-2b and eu-west-1 as temporary failover, 3) net-eng to confirm whether this is host-level NIC issue or AZ backbone.
Ben Ortiz: +1 on routing. I'm going to flip the weighted-route policy for inference.redwoodapi.com to prefer us-west-2b (75%) and us-west-2c (25%) for 2m, then monitor. Will do a gradual shift to avoid cache cold-start storm.
Carla Nguyen: Heads up: if we shift all traffic, KV cache miss rate will spike and increase token cost. We'll enable prefix caching for top prompt sets and warm the models. Running warmup curls across a subset.
deploy-bot: deploy 2041.2 started by Ben Ortiz — update route weight for inference.redwoodapi.com -> us-west-2b:75 us-west-2c:25 (change-id: route-2041.2).
Ben Ortiz: route change pushed. HTTP 502s down from 18% to 9% in the first 30s. Latency p95 improved from 1.2s to 650ms. Still seeing some connection resets for specific instance subnets.
Carla Nguyen: We're seeing model-serving pods in us-west-2a hitting ENI attach failures intermittently. kubelet logs show "failed to update cni config: write: broken pipe" — likely node network plane instability.
Dinesh Patel: Can we fail open to lighter-weight model variants for affected customers to preserve availability? e.g., switch model config to quantized-2b for non-enterprise routes.
Alice Chen: Yes, initiate fallback policy for non-SLA routes. Carla, coordinate toggle. Ben, keep routing in gradual mode. Iris, notify the flagged customers that we're mitigating and expect improved perf in ~10-15m.
Carla Nguyen: Toggling fallback to quantized-2b for public tier now. Command: PATCH /route-configs/inference?fallback_model=quantized-2b — done. Observing reduced CPU on affected pods.
Iris Morgan: Sent update to customers: "We've detected regional network issues impacting inference in us-west-2a. Traffic is being routed to other AZs and lighter model variants for interim mitigation. We're monitoring and will update in 30m."
Ben Ortiz: Net-eng — @Ben Ortiz -> @Alice Chen @Carla Nguyen — I'm seeing increased packet drop between host 10.0.12.* and the AZ gateway at 12:05:10 UTC, consistent with noisy network instance. Raising to AWS support in parallel.
Ben Ortiz: AWS ticket opened: 1234567891 — severity elevated. They confirm noisy host isolation attempt and are migrating underlying hardware. ETA unclear.
Carla Nguyen: We're prepping canary traffic back to us-west-2a once ENI resets subside. For now keep route weight at 75/25. Also enabling aggressive request retries at the proxy layer (2 retries, short backoff) to smooth transient RSTs.
Alice Chen: On-call handoff: @Alice Chen handing to @Carla Nguyen at 12:20 UTC for next 2 hours. Carla, you're primary. Iris, keep comms. Ben, follow up with AWS. Dinesh, watch customer quality metrics.
Carla Nguyen: Taking over. Assigning incident role: lead. Creating incident doc in /incidents/2041234567 with initial timeline and mitigation notes.
Ben Ortiz: AWS updated: noisy NIC detected on host; they started host evacuation at 12:12 UTC. Instance AZ network path expected to recover once eviction completes.
Carla Nguyen: Metrics show steady improvement: 5xx down to 3%, p95 back to ~320ms. We'll wait 15m after AWS completes evacuation before rebalancing weight back to us-west-2a.
Iris Morgan: Customer update posted to status.redwood.com with note about AWS host maintenance and cross-AZ routing mitigation.
Dinesh Patel: Watching evals for quality regression after fallback to quantized models — so far sampling looks acceptable for public tier. Fileting a regression job for top-20 prompts.
Alice Chen: Final note before I drop off: ensure we add runbook item for noisy-host detection -> automatic weighted-route shift + fallback-model toggle to reduce manual toil. Marking P1 but business impact tracking shows no SLA breaches for enterprise customers so far.
Carla Nguyen: Incident transitioning into monitoring mode. I'll close this thread after 90m if metrics remain stable. Thanks all. :tada:
